chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from al-Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
"The young girl is not considered mature (baligh) until she reaches seven years of age."
ai.seo_question: At what age is a young girl considered mature in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Book of Al-Makasib in Tahdhib al-Ahkam establishes a legal ruling regarding the age of maturity (bulugh) for a young girl (jariyah), stating she is not considered mature until she reaches seven years. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration is often cited in discussions concerning the financial capacity (ahliyyah) of minors to engage in commerce or hold property, distinguishing between physical puberty and legal accountability. The specific mention of 'seven years' highlights a foundational threshold in early childhood development within Islamic legal theory.
